title: Silver and gold I have none (Acts 3:1–10)
hook: but what I have, I give thee: rise and walk

segments.voice: Yesterday, Peter's first sermon at Pentecost. Your line was the coward preached.

Anyone who drives knows the little calculation at a red light when someone with a cardboard sign walks between the cars. Do I have cash? Is the light about to change? Do I look, or keep my eyes on the dashboard? Usually the eyes win. Looking is the hard part. Afternoon in Jerusalem, three o'clock, the hour of prayer. Peter and John are walking up to the temple. At one of the gates, a man who has never walked in his life is being set down, the way he is every day, to ask for money.
screen: `THE RED-LIGHT CALCULATION.` → `THREE O'CLOCK, THE HOUR OF PRAYER.` → `A MAN AT THE GATE.`

segments.voice: Luke says he was lame from his mother's womb, carried every day to the gate of the temple called Beautiful, to beg from people going in. He sees Peter and John and asks for alms, the way he asks everyone. Then something unusual happens. Peter, with John, fixes his eyes on him and says, look at us. The man looks up, expecting a coin. And Peter says, in the Douay-Rheims: "Silver and gold I have none; but what I have, I give thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, arise, and walk." Peter takes him by the right hand and lifts him up, and the man's feet and ankles grow strong. He jumps up, stands, walks, and goes into the temple with them, walking and leaping and praising God. Everyone recognizes him: the one from the gate. Notice the order. First, eye contact: look at us. Before anything is given, the man is seen. Then an honest no: I don't have money. Then what Peter does have, which isn't his own: the name of Jesus. Peter's not pretending to be richer than he is, or poorer either. There's a story people tell about Thomas Aquinas visiting the pope while gold was being counted. The pope said, the Church can no longer say silver and gold I have none. And Thomas answered, no, and neither can she say, rise and walk. Nobody can confirm it happened. But it's stuck around for centuries because it names the temptation in today's line.
screen: `THE GATE CALLED BEAUTIFUL.` · `FIRST: LOOK AT US.` · `NO GOLD, BUT WHAT I HAVE.` · `AQUINAS AND THE COUNTED GOLD.` · then, large: `SILVER AND GOLD I HAVE NONE.`

segments.voice: Rest your hands open on your lap and ask what you can give today, not money, necessarily: time, a skill, a car with an empty seat, a listening ear, a language you speak, a kind word, your full attention. Name two or three things quietly, and picture one person who needs one of them. If you pray, hold Peter's words, what I have, I give thee, and offer it; if you don't, just keep your hands open.
Beautiful. The gate of the temple where a man who had never walked begged every day, until Peter said, what I have, I give thee: arise and walk. Today's word.
Your line: what I have I give. It started with a look. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics are taught the corporal and spiritual works of mercy, giving not only money but time, care, counsel and prayer to people in need.

chat.says: Peter had no money for the beggar. So what did he actually give him?
options: First a look, then what he had: in the name of Jesus, arise and walk.
A promise to come back with money once the prayers were over.
Some bread and kind words, since he had no coins to hand over.
chat.meaning: Peter looks at him, admits he has no silver or gold, then gives what he has: the name of Jesus. The man walks.
